title.en: Kirchhoff's rules and the Wheatstone bridge

hook.en: Series and parallel rules fail for many networks. Kirchhoff gave two rules, one from conservation of charge and one from conservation of energy, that solve all of them.
hook.kn: ಶ್ರೇಣಿ ಮತ್ತು ಸಮಾಂತರ ನಿಯಮಗಳು ಅನೇಕ ಜಾಲಗಳಿಗೆ ಸಾಲುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಆವೇಶ ಸಂರಕ್ಷಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ಶಕ್ತಿ ಸಂರಕ್ಷಣೆಯಿಂದ ಬಂದ ಕಿರ್ಕಾಫ್‌ನ ಎರಡು ನಿಯಮಗಳು ಎಲ್ಲವನ್ನೂ ಬಿಡಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

objectives.en: State and apply Kirchhoff's junction and loop rules.
Derive and use the balance condition of a Wheatstone bridge.

narration.en: Series and parallel rules fail for many networks. Kirchhoff gave two rules, one from conservation of charge and one from conservation of energy, that solve all of them.
narration.kn: ಶ್ರೇಣಿ ಮತ್ತು ಸಮಾಂತರ ನಿಯಮಗಳು ಅನೇಕ ಜಾಲಗಳಿಗೆ ಸಾಲುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಆವೇಶ ಸಂರಕ್ಷಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ಶಕ್ತಿ ಸಂರಕ್ಷಣೆಯಿಂದ ಬಂದ ಕಿರ್ಕಾಫ್‌ನ ಎರಡು ನಿಯಮಗಳು ಎಲ್ಲವನ್ನೂ ಬಿಡಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

body.en: Junction rule: at any junction the sum of currents entering equals the sum of currents leaving (conservation of charge). Loop rule: around any closed loop the algebraic sum of changes in potential is zero (conservation of energy). Sign convention: crossing a resistor in the direction of the current, the potential falls by IR; crossing a cell from − to +, it rises by ε.
body.kn: ಸಂಧಿ ನಿಯಮ: ಸಂಧಿಗೆ ಬರುವ ಪ್ರವಾಹ = ಹೊರಹೋಗುವ ಪ್ರವಾಹ (ಆವೇಶ ಸಂರಕ್ಷಣೆ). ಕುಣಿಕೆ ನಿಯಮ: ಯಾವುದೇ ಮುಚ್ಚಿದ ಕುಣಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ವಿಭವ ಬದಲಾವಣೆಗಳ ಮೊತ್ತ ಶೂನ್ಯ (ಶಕ್ತಿ ಸಂರಕ್ಷಣೆ).

points.en: Along the current through R: −IR; through a cell − to +: +ε

narration.en: Junction rule: current in equals current out, from conservation of charge. Loop rule: the potential changes around any closed loop add to zero, from conservation of energy.
narration.kn: ಸಂಧಿ ನಿಯಮ: ಸಂಧಿಗೆ ಬರುವ ಪ್ರವಾಹ = ಹೊರಹೋಗುವ ಪ್ರವಾಹ (ಆವೇಶ ಸಂರಕ್ಷಣೆ). ಕುಣಿಕೆ ನಿಯಮ: ಯಾವುದೇ ಮುಚ್ಚಿದ ಕುಣಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ವಿಭವ ಬದಲಾವಣೆಗಳ ಮೊತ್ತ ಶೂನ್ಯ (ಶಕ್ತಿ ಸಂರಕ್ಷಣೆ).

title.en: On the board: Kirchhoff's rules and the Wheatstone bridge

narration.en: Junction rule: the current flowing into a junction equals the current flowing out, because charge is conserved. Loop rule: round any closed loop, the emfs add up to the sum of the IR drops, because energy is conserved. In a Wheatstone bridge four resistors P, Q, R and S form a diamond, with a galvanometer across the middle. At balance no current flows through G, and then P over Q equals R over S. Example: P = 10 Ω, Q = 20 Ω and R = 15 Ω, so S = QR/P = 30 Ω.

say.en: Junction rule: the current flowing into a junction equals the current flowing out, because charge is conserved.
Loop rule: round any closed loop, the emfs add up to the sum of the IR drops, because energy is conserved.
In a Wheatstone bridge four resistors P, Q, R and S form a diamond, with a galvanometer across the middle.
At balance no current flows through G, and then P over Q equals R over S.
Example: P = 10 Ω, Q = 20 Ω and R = 15 Ω, so S = QR/P = 30 Ω.

body.en: Four resistors P, Q, R and S form a diamond; a cell is connected across one diagonal and a galvanometer across the other. Applying Kirchhoff's rules, the galvanometer current is zero (the bridge is balanced) when $P/Q = R/S$. The galvanometer arm can then be ignored, and an unknown resistance can be found from the other three.
body.kn: ವೀಟ್‌ಸ್ಟೋನ್ ಸೇತುವೆಯಲ್ಲಿ P/Q = R/S ಆದಾಗ ಗ್ಯಾಲ್ವನೋಮೀಟರ್ ಮೂಲಕ ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಶೂನ್ಯ (ಸಮತೋಲನ). ಆಗ ಅಜ್ಞಾತ ರೋಧವನ್ನು ಉಳಿದ ಮೂರರಿಂದ ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿಯಬಹುದು.

points.en: At balance the galvanometer arm carries no current

narration.en: In a Wheatstone bridge, no current flows through the galvanometer when P by Q equals R by S. Then an unknown resistance can be found from the other three.
narration.kn: ವೀಟ್‌ಸ್ಟೋನ್ ಸೇತುವೆಯಲ್ಲಿ P/Q = R/S ಆದಾಗ ಗ್ಯಾಲ್ವನೋಮೀಟರ್ ಮೂಲಕ ಪ್ರವಾಹ ಶೂನ್ಯ (ಸಮತೋಲನ). ಆಗ ಅಜ್ಞಾತ ರೋಧವನ್ನು ಉಳಿದ ಮೂರರಿಂದ ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿಯಬಹುದು.

aim.en: To verify Kirchhoff's current law and voltage law in a network with two sources.

narration.en: Measure the three branch currents at a junction and check that current in equals current out. Then go round each loop and check that the voltage rises equal the voltage drops.

caption.en: A 6 V cell across A and C. The curve shows the voltage across the galvanometer, V_B − V_D, as S changes; it crosses zero at balance.

tryThis.en: Set P = 10, Q = 20, R = 15: the curve crosses zero at S = 30 Ω.
Move S to 30 Ω: the galvanometer voltage is zero.
Swap P and Q: the balance point moves. Why?

narration.en: A 6 V cell across A and C. The curve shows the voltage across the galvanometer, V_B − V_D, as S changes; it crosses zero at balance. Set P = 10, Q = 20, R = 15: the curve crosses zero at S = 30 Ω. Move S to 30 Ω: the galvanometer voltage is zero. Swap P and Q: the balance point moves. Why?

problem.en: Cells of 12 V and 6 V (no internal resistance), each in series with a 2 Ω resistor, are joined in parallel (positive terminals together) across a 4 Ω resistor. Find the current in each branch.

steps.en: Let I₁ and I₂ flow up through the 12 V and 6 V branches; I₁ + I₂ flows through the 4 Ω (junction rule).
Loop 1: 12 = 2I₁ + 4(I₁ + I₂), so 6I₁ + 4I₂ = 12. Loop 2: 6 = 2I₂ + 4(I₁ + I₂), so 4I₁ + 6I₂ = 6.
Solving: I₁ = 2.4 A, I₂ = −0.6 A, and the 4 Ω carries 1.8 A.

answer.en: 2.4 A through the 12 V cell; 0.6 A flowing backwards through the 6 V cell (it is being charged); 1.8 A through the 4 Ω

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Cells of 12 V and 6 V (no internal resistance), each in series with a 2 Ω resistor, are joined in parallel (positive terminals together) across a 4 Ω resistor. Find the current in each branch.

problem.en: In a balanced Wheatstone bridge, P = 10 Ω, Q = 20 Ω and R = 15 Ω. Find S.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. In a balanced Wheatstone bridge, P = 10 Ω, Q = 20 Ω and R = 15 Ω. Find S.

body.en: A bridge is balanced when the products of opposite arms are equal: P × S = Q × R. Once balanced, delete the middle resistor or galvanometer and solve the circuit as two series pairs in parallel.

narration.en: Balanced bridge: cross products equal. A bridge is balanced when the products of opposite arms are equal: P × S = Q × R. Once balanced, delete the middle resistor or galvanometer and solve the circuit as two series pairs in parallel.
